page: Amazon Web Services c8i.metal-96xl is a bare-metal, compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It features dual Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors delivering 192 physical cores and 384 dedicated vCPUs operating at a 3.9 GHz clock frequency. The architecture incorporates 480 MB of shared L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). System memory consists of 768 GB of DDR5 operating at 7 GHz, providing a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per physical core. The bare-metal platform lacks bundled local storage, requiring network-attached solutions, and provides a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

In benchmark testing, the high core count and vector extensions achieve top-tier multi-threaded performance. The instance scored 417,805.84 in stress-ng multi-core tests, 181,125.91 in PassMark CPU tests, and 65,530.0 in Geekbench Clang compilation. Cryptographic and extended instruction benchmarks ranked in the top 10%, supported by hardware-level VAES and AMX instructions. Memory bandwidth exceeded 1,170 GB/s for large uncached reads, enabling top-tier throughput in Redis operations (510.74 million operations per second) and static web serving (178.42 GB/s). However, single-threaded performance registers in the middle tier, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2,140.9, and CPU-only LLM token generation rates remain limited compared to GPU-equipped alternatives.

From an infrastructure standpoint, the c8i.metal-96xl delivers massive compute density and bare-metal execution without hypervisor overhead, maximizing resource yield per physical node for highly parallel workloads. The primary tradeoff lies in the absence of local NVMe storage and the compute-skewed 2:1 vCPU-to-memory allocation, which restricts applicability for memory-bloated databases. This server is best suited for compute-intensive batch processing, software compilation clusters, high-throughput web serving, distributed CI/CD builds, and high-performance computing simulations requiring dense integer and vector compute.

It provides 192 physical cores and 384 dedicated vCPUs clocked at 3.9 GHz, backed by 480 MB of L3 cache, AVX-512, and AMX instruction sets. Memory capacity stands at 768 GB of DDR5 running at 7 GHz, paired with 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and no local storage. Benchmark results highlight top-tier multi-threaded processing, leading scores in PassMark CPU suites, Clang compilation, and in-memory key-value throughput exceeding 510 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-thread execution is moderate and LLM generation lacks GPU acceleration, its dense compute profile delivers high throughput efficiency for parallel tasks. The c8i.metal-96xl is purpose-built for CPU-intensive parallel computing, large-scale software builds, batch data crunching, and high-throughput network serving.
